title: Bar graphs: the whole and the missing part

beats.say: Each dot stands for one tree. The trees are sorted into three kinds: oak, pine and maple.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: How many trees are shown altogether across the three categories?
One dot stands for one tree.

beats.say: A category is one kind. Oak is a category. Altogether asks for every tree in all the categories.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Category = kind. Altogether = in all.

beats.say: The numbers up the side form the scale. They tell how many trees each height means.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Start at zero. Two equal steps reach two, so each step up counts one tree.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: One step up = one tree.

beats.say: Draw a rectangle around each pile. These rectangles are bars. Together they make a bar graph.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The dots can fade. A bar keeps the pile's height, so it still tells how many trees.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: I counted each picture before. Could I count these three bars and say three trees?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Three counts the categories. Look inside the bars: each one stands for several trees.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: 3 categories

beats.say: Oak reaches three. Pine reaches five. Maple reaches two.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: To find the total, the number in all, bring all the dots together. Count each tree once.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Three oak trees and two maple trees fill one row of five.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The five pine trees fill the other row. Five plus five is ten.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Three is how many kinds. Ten is how many trees altogether.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: This graph shows oak, pine and maple trees. How many trees are shown altogether across the three categories?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: How many trees are shown altogether across the three categories?

beats.say: The scale has a line for every one tree. The printed numbers go zero, two, four, and so on.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Oak's top meets six. There are six oak trees.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Oak: 6

beats.say: Pine ends between the printed six and eight. Which number do I use?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: From six, move up one step. That line means seven, even without a printed seven.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Pine: 7

beats.say: Maple ends one step above ten. That is eleven maple trees.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Maple: 11

beats.say: These dots stand for the same six, seven and eleven trees. Put those counts together.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Each pair of rows has ten places. Move the same dots here; no tree is added or lost.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Move the six oak dots first. Then the seven pine dots.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Bring the eleven maple dots too. Every tree is counted once.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The first two rows hold ten. The next two make twenty. Four more gives twenty-four.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Six plus seven plus eleven gives the total: twenty-four trees.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The total includes every group. Twenty-four trees can be more than the top number on the graph.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: The bar graph shows the pets of thirteen students. Each student has one pet.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: 13 students. Each has one pet. The dog bar is not drawn yet. How many students have a dog?

beats.say: The dog bar is not drawn yet. How many students have a dog?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: There is no dog bar. Does that mean no one has a dog?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Not drawn yet means unknown. Zero would mean we know there are none. Use the thirteen students to find out.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Not drawn yet = count unknown.

beats.say: One pet for each student means one group for each student. Each dot is one student.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: The whole is 13 students.

beats.say: Cat reaches five, one step above four. Fish reaches four.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Place five of the thirteen students in the cat bar, and four in the fish bar.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Five plus four is nine students placed. The dots left below must belong in the missing dog group.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Should I add the thirteen students to the nine?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: The thirteen already includes those nine. We separated them from the whole. We need only the students left.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Count on from nine: ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen. Four more students complete the whole.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Taking the nine known students from thirteen leaves four. Thirteen minus nine equals four.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The dog bar must reach four. Four students have a dog.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Check every group: five plus four plus four is thirteen. All thirteen students have a place.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: A scale can count in bigger steps. How many oak trees does this bar show?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: How many oak trees does this bar show?

beats.say: Read this scale: zero, two, four, six. Each step up counts two trees.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: I see three steps, with two trees in each. Two, four, six trees.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: The six dots confirm it. Always read what a step counts before reading the bars.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Read the scale before the bars.

beats.say: This graph shows thirteen students' pets. Each student has one pet. The fish bar is not drawn yet.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: 13 students. Each has one pet. The fish bar is not drawn yet. How many students have a fish?

beats.say: How many students have a fish? Champ, what does the scale tell you?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Two steps go from zero to two, so each step is one pet. Dog reaches two.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Cat is one step above two: three. Bird is one step above four: five.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Each student has one pet. Two plus three is five. Five plus five is ten students in the drawn bars.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Where is the whole?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Thirteen is the whole, including those ten. I need the students left for fish.
beats.speaker: learner

do.text: Whole: 13. Placed: 10.

beats.say: Ten and three more make thirteen. Thirteen minus ten is three, so three students have a fish.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: How can you check?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Put every group back together. Two plus three plus five plus three is thirteen. Every student is included once.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: The height tells how many are in a group. First I read what one step counts.
beats.speaker: learner

do.text: Read the scale, then each bar's height.

beats.say: If the total is missing, I put all the groups together.
beats.speaker: learner

do.text: Total unknown: add all the groups.

beats.say: If the total is given, I take out the known groups. What is left fills the missing bar.
beats.speaker: learner

do.text: Group unknown: total minus known groups.

beats.say: I check that every group together makes the whole.
beats.speaker: learner

do.text: Check: all groups together make the whole.
